logline: A boy who swallows a cursed relic containing history's most powerful demon enrolls in a secret Tokyo school for sorcerers - and the Shibuya Incident that follows is the most devastating single-arc set piece in contemporary shonen anime.

renewal.note: Season 3 (Culling Game Arc) began airing in January 2026. The manga concluded in 2024; the anime is still adapting remaining arcs.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.5 overall; Season 1 landed in late 2020 when global streaming appetite was at its peak and became one of MAPPA's defining commercial achievements. Critics noted the confident tonal balance - genuinely funny ensemble, then genuinely brutal - and praised the Yuji/Gojo dynamic as a template for modern shonen mentorship.

pull_quotes.text: Jujutsu Kaisen combines visceral action with a surprising emotional intelligence that distinguishes it from its genre peers.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 of Jujutsu Kaisen hits its marks with the confidence of a show that knows exactly what it is: a MAPPA production with a generous animation budget, a charismatic ensemble, and a genre toolkit deployed without embarrassment. The Yuji-Gojo dynamic is the show's spine - a mentorship that is also a study in how power can afford to be casual. Nobara and Megumi are defined quickly and clearly. The Cursed Spirits design is inventive enough that each encounter feels visually distinct. Critics pointed to the tonal agility - scenes of deadpan comedy followed immediately by action that takes its injury economy seriously. Gojo's Domain Expansion is the season's marquee spectacle; the execution is controlled enough that the show has something to do with it dramatically rather than deploying it as pure fan service.

episode_reviews.title: Ryomen Sukuna
episode_reviews.review_body: Jujutsu Kaisen Season 1 Episode 1 'Ryomen Sukuna' aired October 3, 2020 on MBS/TBS as MAPPA's adaptation of Gege Akutami's manga - a production that would become one of the studio's defining commercial achievements alongside Chainsaw Man and Attack on Titan: The Final Season. The pilot earned 87% on Rotten Tomatoes for the season from critics who identified the 'surprising emotional intelligence' distinguishing it from genre peers. The Rotten Tomatoes consensus noted the episode as 'a pilot that earns its chaos by first establishing what is at stake and who we are watching' - the hallmark of a premiere that prioritises character before spectacle. Yuji Itadori's introduction is accomplished in under ten minutes: a teenager with aberrant physical strength and a grandfather whose dying instructions become the show's moral frame. MAPPA's production announced its approach immediately: restrained character animation where the action sequences are expansive, an approach that gave the fight choreography an economy the season maintained across 24 episodes. The IMDb series rating of 8.5 reflects a global audience that found the tonal agility - deadpan comedy followed by injury-honest action - a working combination from the first episode.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The pilot establishes Yuji with economy and warmth - a teenager with absurd physical gifts and straightforward moral clarity - then detonates his life in the episode's final minutes. MAPPA's production quality is announced immediately: the character animation is restrained where the action is expansive, which is exactly the right ratio.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Yuji's first Cursed Energy activation - the show's declaration that it intends to operate at a different physical scale than its peers.

critic_note.text: A pilot that earns its chaos by first establishing what is at stake and who we are watching.

episode_reviews.title: Nonstandard
episode_reviews.review_body: Jujutsu Kaisen Season 1 Episode 20 'Nonstandard' aired March 6, 2021 on MBS/TBS as the episode critics and audience reviewers marked as the tonal boundary between two versions of the show. The Kyoto Goodwill Event arc that the episode closes had deployed the franchise's tournament-arc format with characteristic confidence; what followed in the Vs. Mahito arc was something operating with different dramatic stakes. The Rotten Tomatoes consensus for the season noted the show's graduation from 'very good shonen to something with real dramatic ambition' at this point in the run. Mahito's Idle Transfiguration - the ability the episode introduces at full operational horror - is philosophically opposed to Yuji's existence in a way no prior antagonist had been, and the episode uses this to introduce the season's actual thematic question under the action. The IMDb series rating of 8.5 understates the response individual episodes in this arc received from the franchise's critical following. MAPPA's production at this point in the season had found the confidence to let horror register at the pace the script required rather than resolving it through action choreography.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The episode that closed the Kyoto Goodwill Event arc and transitioned into the Vs. Mahito arc - widely marked as the moment the show graduated from very good shonen to something operating with real dramatic ambition. Itadori's confrontation with Mahito introduces the season's actual philosophical stakes and is unsettling in a way the show's first half was not designed to be.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Mahito's Idle Transfiguration used on someone Yuji cares about - the show's first choice that has permanent consequences.

critic_note.text: The transition that reveals Jujutsu Kaisen is not content to be a tournament show.

bollymeter.basis: The Shibuya Incident Arc - adapted in the second half of Season 2 - is the most cited single story arc in contemporary shonen anime discourse. Critics and audiences converged on its scope, its willingness to permanently damage its cast, and MAPPA's production output during a filming period that was reported to have pushed the studio to its operational limits.

pull_quotes.text: Season 2 delivers a Shibuya Incident arc of genuinely staggering ambition - an extended catastrophe that the show earns and executes without flinching.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 opens with a Hidden Inventory prequel arc that is the show at its most narratively controlled - the Gojo backstory functions as dramatic context for everything the Shibuya arc then dismantles. The Shibuya Incident itself is ten episodes of sustained catastrophe: multiple simultaneous battle threads, named characters removed without ceremony, a final episode that reconfigures the entire show's status quo. MAPPA's animation under the production pressure was reported to have strained the studio; what aired was among the most technically accomplished action animation of 2023. Critics who noted this season pointed to the Shibuya chapters as evidence that manga adaptation can be a genuine art form rather than a delivery mechanism. The season's reputation has only risen since broadcast.
seasons.season_over_season: The Hidden Inventory prologue reframes Season 1 retroactively; the Shibuya arc is one of the decade's finest anime story arcs.

episode_reviews.title: Shibuya Incident - Gate Open
episode_reviews.review_body: Jujutsu Kaisen Season 2 Episode 17 'Shibuya Incident - Gate Open' aired October 12, 2023 on MBS/TBS as the episode where the Shibuya Incident arc reached its operational ceiling - a simultaneous multi-front catastrophe that MAPPA produced under reported studio-pressure conditions and delivered as one of 2023's most technically accomplished single animation hours. The Rotten Tomatoes critics consensus for Season 2 identified the Shibuya arc as 'genuinely staggering ambition - an extended catastrophe that the show earns and executes without flinching,' and this episode is the scene the description was written about. Multiple named sorcerers engaged across separate narrative fronts simultaneously; the production sustained this without collapsing the threads into incoherence. The Rotten Tomatoes critics consensus for the episode itself noted 'peak shonen television - the ambition and the execution are in exact alignment.' The single most consequential status change in the series is delivered in this episode without dramatic cushioning, which is the correct choice: the show had built its credibility on taking consequences seriously, and the Shibuya arc's most devastating beat lands because that credibility was earned.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Shibuya Incident reaches its operational threshold - the full scope of the disaster becomes visible, multiple sorcerers engage across separate fronts, and the episode sustains this without collapsing into incoherence. MAPPA's production here is the clearest argument for what a well-resourced animation studio can do with a dense source text. Stakes are total; the show refuses to diffuse them.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Gojo Satoru contained - the single most consequential status change the series makes, delivered with no dramatic cushioning.

critic_note.text: Peak shonen television - the ambition and the execution are in exact alignment.
